title: Beset with Snares on Every Hand
description: Beset with Snares on Every Hand in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 455 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Choosing the Better Part”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Be-set with snares on ev-ery hand, In life's un-cer-tain path I stand: Fa-ther di-vine! dif-fuse thy light, To guide my doubt-ful foot-steps right.

lines: Beset with snares on every hand,
In life's uncertain path I stand:
To guide my doubtful footsteps right.
Wisely to choose the better part;
To scorn the trifles of a day,
For joys that none can take away.
Then let the wildest storms arise,
Let tempests mingle earth with skies,
No fatal shipwreck shall I fear,
But all my treasures with me bear.
If thou, my Saviour, still be nigh,
Cheerful I live, and joyful die;
To find ten thousand worlds in thee.

licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
